title: Nanda Empire
capsule: The Nanda Empire was the most extensive pre-Mauryan state of northern India, ruling from Pataliputra over the Gangetic plains and reportedly commanding a vast army — ancient sources cite 200,000 infantry, 20,000 cavalry, 2,000 chariots, and 3,000–6,000 war elephants — which deterred Alexander the Great's forces at the Hyphasis (Beas) River in 325 BCE. Founded by Mahapadma Nanda, who overthrew the Shishunaga dynasty, the empire extended its tributary control from Bengal to the Punjab. The last Nanda ruler, Dhana Nanda, was overthrown around 321 BCE by Chandragupta Maurya with the counsel of Kautilya (Chanakya), inaugurating the Maurya Empire.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The empire's extent is reconstructed from Puranic genealogies, Greek accounts of Alexander's campaign, and Jain and Buddhist texts; no inscriptional evidence from the Nanda period survives and territorial boundaries are conjectural.
